subject: Discovery recap: Novus Health model-quality delta & validation checklist
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-08-21T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap: Novus Health model-quality delta & validation checklist

Sam — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick written recap + proposed validation checklist so we have clear next steps. Attaching a short recording and the draft MAA we discussed.

Call highlights:
- Novus primary use case: clinical note summarization + triage flags (high cost of hallucinations).
- Target throughput: 120 concurrent requests during business hours; p95 latency goal ~350ms.
- Existing baseline: hyperscaler A (vendorA.ai) in production for last 6 months — you're seeing intermittent hallucination bursts on out-of-domain clinical prompts.

Competitive notes from today (high level):
- Redwood Inference: focused runtime batching + prefix caching should reduce per-token cost vs hyperscaler A for long-context notes; model routing gives a predictable fallback path when load spikes.
- Hyperscaler A: good for throughput but we saw higher hallucination rates in our internal probes on clinical instructions.
- Hyperscaler B: stronger safety filtering but higher latencies and variability at scale.

Proposed validation checklist (what we'll run next week):
1) Hallucination probe suite (legal/clinical prompts) — 1k prompts, measure hallucination rate and severity. Owner: Redwood SE (Marissa).
2) Regression check against your canonical prompt set (20 seed prompts) — compare token-by-token deltas and semantic score. Owner: Novus + Redwood.
3) Latency & cost baseline at expected traffic profile (120 concurrent) — p50/p95, per-1000-token cost.
4) Failover/fallback exercise — simulate reduced capacity and confirm graceful degradation.

Deliverables and timeline:
- Wed 2026-08-25: we deliver an eval-prompts bundle and run plan.
- Fri 2026-08-28: initial probe results (hallucination + latency).
- Week of 2026-08-31: A/B runs vs Hyperscaler A (and Hyperscaler B if you want) and a short findings doc.

Acceptance criteria draft (open for your input):
- Hallucination rate on clinical-critical prompts <= 1.5% (severity-weighted).
- No more than 2% regression in semantic-similarity score vs your baseline set.
- p95 latency under 450ms under target load.

Attachments: call-recording-20260821.mp4 (audio), novus-maa-draft.pdf (draft MAA).

Next steps: can you confirm the sample prompts export (if available) and whether you want both Hyperscaler A and Hyperscaler B included in the A/B comparisons? If yes, please share access credentials or a test account and any redaction rules for PHI.

Thanks — looking forward.

—

Aditya — thanks for the clear recap. This aligns with what we discussed. A few quick answers:

- I'll attach a CSV with ~200 sanitized sample prompts that represent our most sensitive clinical workflows (see attached: novus-sample-prompts.csv).
- Yes please include Hyperscaler A in the A/B comparison; we can consider Hyperscaler B if the initial deltas are inconclusive.
- Acceptance criteria: clinical team prefers hallucination <= 1% on the most-critical subset, but we can be pragmatic on broader prompts. If Redwood's severity-weighted approach requires <1.5% that's a reasonable starting point.

Question for Marissa: can you confirm the exact hallucination definition/annotation instructions you'll use? The clinical team will provide two clinicians for annotation over 3 days if that helps.

Best,
Sam

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Novus Health model-quality delta & validation checklist

Great call. Sam — thanks for the sample prompts; this helps a lot. Below is a concrete test matrix and annotation plan so the run has measurable, reproducible criteria.

Test matrix (high level):
- Arms: Redwood Inference (model family pinned to redwood-1.5), Hyperscaler A (vendorA-1.4), Hyperscaler B (vendorB-2.0) [Hyperscaler B only if requested].
- Data: Novus-sample-prompts.csv (200 sanitized prompts) + critical-20 seed prompts for regression checks.
- Runs: 3 iterations per arm for sampling stability; temperature and sampling params matched to your production configs.

Evaluation metrics and acceptance criteria:
- Hallucination rate (binary per-response) + severity-weighted score (0–3). Threshold: <=1.5% severity-weighted for production-readiness; <=1.0% on the critical-20 subset if Novus requires it.
- Factuality F1 (when ground-truth exists) — no more than 2% drop vs baseline.
- Semantic similarity (embedding cosine, mean similarity) — regression <= 2%.
- Latency: p50/p95 under target load — p95 target <= 450ms.
- Cost: per-1k-token comparison and per-session cost at expected throughput.

Annotation instructions (what we'll ask clinicians to mark):
1) Was any assertion in the response not supported by the prompt/context? (Y/N)
2) If Y, how severe is the incorrect assertion (1 = minor, 3 = clinically dangerous).
3) Is the response actionable vs. too vague? (Y/N)

We will provide: eval-prompts-v1.txt (cleaned prompts for the SE pipeline), and a regression-matrix.xlsx (expected columns for automated scoring). Marissa will run the first automated pass; we can onboard your two clinicians to the annotator UI (3-day annotation window recommended).

Operational notes:
- For Hyperscaler A runs we'll use their test endpoint (please provide a test key or short-term account).
- We will strip any residual PHI and run in a private evaluation VPC; results and logs will be shared via the secure drive link.

I can start the automated runs tomorrow afternoon and aim to hand off the clinician annotation bundle by EOD Wed.

Attachments: eval-prompts-v1.txt, regression-matrix.xlsx

—
